document.title: Verification Card Architectural Recommendation: Read-Display + Action-Dispatch Pattern
document.context: Business Hub · UHN Research · AAR Module
document.responds_to: Verification Framework strategy proposal (discussion draft, in response to PRD v1.1 / ADR-001)
document.summary: The c-verification-card LWC should be a read-only display component with action-dispatch capability — NOT an inline editor. All data modifications must route through Salesforce-native write paths (Flows, modals, record pages) where validation rules, FLS, sharing, and audit logging are enforced by the platform.

recommendation.principle: Verification ≠ Editing. The card displays verification state and dispatches state-transition actions. It never writes to records directly.
rationale: The Verification Framework's entire value proposition is provenance — 'System says X' vs 'PI attested to X after review' are legally and institutionally different statements. Inline editing on the verification card collapses that boundary.

Research Strategy exports to CIHR, Tri-Council, and rankings need to answer 'was this value PI-attested or system-suggested?' — the answer stops being clean if the attestation surface is also the editing surface.
A PI clicking 'Verify' is a specific legal and institutional claim: 'I reviewed what the system suggested and I confirm it.' That is a state transition, not a data edit.

Salesforce-native security (OWD, FLS, sharing rules, validation rules) enforces write constraints automatically through standard DML. A custom LWC inline editor would need to re-implement or mirror those constraints — creating a maintenance liability and a security surface that doesn't need to exist.

MUST_DO.detail: Show Proposed / Verified / Manual / Superseded status with visual differentiation (colour-coded badges or sidebar indicators per the framework mockup)
MUST_DO.implementation: Read Verification_Status__c (or Record Type, depending on adoption decision) via @wire getRecord

MUST_DO.detail: Show verifier's name, not raw User ID. Display Verified_By__c as a resolved name and Verified_At__c as a formatted timestamp.
MUST_DO.implementation: Use getRecord with Verified_By__r.Name or a lightweight Apex controller that returns the resolved name

MUST_DO.capability: Show source system and override indicators
MUST_DO.detail: Display Source_System__c origin. On Verified records with PI corrections, show a 'corrected' indicator. Hover/tooltip reveals source value vs PI-corrected value and correction timestamp.
MUST_DO.implementation: If Override_Payload__c JSON pattern is adopted: parse JSON client-side for display diff. If field-level overrides: compare source fields vs current values.

MUST_DO.capability: Offer state-transition actions (Verify / Reject / Verify All)
MUST_DO.detail: Proposed records show a 'Verify' button. Rejected records use soft-delete (Excluded__c = true, Exclusion_Reason__c picklist). 'Verify All' bulk action satisfies SUB-06.
MUST_DO.implementation: Button dispatches to VerificationReconciliationService via Apex invocable or launches BH-1249 Screen Flow. Card does NOT write to the record — it invokes the service/Flow that does.

MUST_DO.detail: When the underlying record changes through any channel (Flow, modal edit, admin action, batch sync), the card refreshes immediately to reflect the new state.
MUST_DO.implementation: Use @wire with refreshApex after Lightning Data Service update, or subscribe to a Lightning Message Service channel that the write path publishes to after commit.

MUST_NOT_DO.reason: Bypasses validation rules (VR_Attestation_Required, VR_Lock_After_Submit, VR_Evaluator_Assessment_Status). Would require re-implementing business logic in JavaScript.

MUST_NOT_DO.prohibition: Direct DML writes to verifiable records
MUST_NOT_DO.reason: Skips the VerificationReconciliationService's change-event logging, override-payload diffing, and hash-reconciliation logic. Writes must go through the service.

FLS and sharing should be enforced by the platform on the write path, not duplicated in the component. The card is read-only, so it only needs to respect field visibility (which @wire handles natively via WITH SECURITY_ENFORCED or stripInaccessible).

After AAR Status = Submitted, the card should be fully inert — no Verify buttons, no edit paths, no action dispatches. Per BH-987 validation and BH-1010 PI permission set: PI records are read-only after submission.

PI.verify_action: Available on Proposed records when AAR Status = Draft or In Progress
PI.edit_path: Data corrections route through AAR Workspace edit modal (standard DML with full validation/FLS)
PI.post_submission: Card is fully inert — no actions available
PI.security_enforcement: BH-1010 PI permission set: Edit own AAR records (Status = Draft or In Progress), Read-only after Submitted

Evaluator.purpose: Verification state helps evaluators understand data provenance (PI-entered vs system-suggested) when reviewing AARs
Evaluator.edit_path: Evaluators interact with their own AAR_Evaluation__c record (BH-1246), not with the verification card
Evaluator.security_enforcement: BH-1010 evaluator permission set: Read ALL AAR records within their Institute, Edit only AAR_Evaluation__c fields (Status = Draft). VR_Evaluator_Assessment_Status blocks assessment on non-Submitted AARs.

Admin.edit_path: Corrections and state resets go through standard record detail page or Setup with Modify All. Full audit trail via field history (BH-1126) and change events.
Admin.rationale: No admin edit mode needed on the card — it reflects whatever the admin changed through standard channels

Institute_Director.purpose: Visibility into verification state across all Institute AAR records
Institute_Director.security_enforcement: BH-1010 sharing rule: Read all AAR records within their Institute via Account-scoped Experience Cloud sharing rule

edit_routing.principle: All data modifications route through Salesforce-native write paths, never through the card

paths.route: Card dispatches → VerificationReconciliationService (Apex) or BH-1249 Screen Flow
paths.what_happens: Record Type transitions Proposed → Verified (or Verification_Status__c updates). Verified_By__c / Verified_At__c captured. Change event written to Verification_Change_Event__c.
Excluded__c = true, Exclusion_Reason__c set via picklist. Change event logged.

paths.action: Correct data on a Verified record
paths.route: PI clicks through to AAR Workspace edit modal → standard record edit
paths.what_happens: If Override_Payload__c pattern adopted: service diffs correction against source, writes JSON override, logs change event, preserves source hash. If direct field edit: validation rules fire natively, field history captures old/new.

paths.route: Card dispatches bulk action → Apex invocable method
paths.what_happens: Batch Proposed → Verified transition. Each record gets Verified_By__c / Verified_At__c. Change events written per record.

paths.route: Standard record detail page with Modify All permission
paths.what_happens: Full audit trail via Shield field history (BH-1126). Change event written if Verification_Status__c changes.

security: Zero component-level security logic — all write constraints enforced by Salesforce platform (OWD Private, sharing rules, FLS, validation rules)
No risk of a LWC bug granting unintended edit access — the card never writes
PI read-only after submission is enforced by the permission set, not by card-level conditional rendering that could be bypassed
audit: Clean provenance boundary: every write goes through a service or Flow that logs to Verification_Change_Event__c
No ambiguity between 'viewed' and 'changed' — the card is display-only, so any change in the audit log came from a deliberate write path
Shield field history (BH-1126) and change events provide two independent audit layers
architecture: Simpler LWC: no dirty-state tracking, no save-error handling, no optimistic UI rollback, no field-level edit permission checks
Single responsibility: the card displays state and dispatches actions; the service/Flow handles business logic and persistence
Testability: the card's behaviour is fully deterministic from the record state — no write-path edge cases to test in the component
business: Institutional trust: PIs cannot accidentally modify data through the verification surface — corrections are deliberate, tracked, and auditable
Export integrity: Research Strategy's CIHR/Tri-Council exports can distinguish 'PI-attested' from 'system-suggested' without ambiguity
Compliance: attestation provenance is never contaminated by inline edits that bypass the verification service

lwc_component_structure.name: c-verification-card
lwc_component_structure.data_access: @wire getRecord for reactive display; refreshApex after action dispatch completes
lwc_component_structure.action_dispatch: Call @AuraEnabled Apex methods (or invoke Flows via lightning/flow) — never call DML from the component directly
lwc_component_structure.user_resolution: Resolve Verified_By__c to Verified_By__r.Name in the wire call or Apex controller

status_rendering.Verified: Full row, 'corrected' badge if Override_Payload__c is non-null, hover shows source diff
status_rendering.Manual: Full row, 'source: manual entry' badge, no action buttons (nothing to verify)
status_rendering.Superseded: Struck-through or collapsed row, 'superseded by [Source_Record_Id__c]' link

lwc_component_structure.conditional_inertness: When parent AAR Status__c IN ('Submitted', 'Under Review', 'Complete'), hide ALL action buttons. Card becomes pure display.

methods_the_card_calls.action: Proposed → Verified transition. Sets Verified_By__c, Verified_At__c, transitions Record Type or Verification_Status__c, writes change event.
Bulk Proposed → Verified. Same logic, bulkified. Satisfies SUB-06.
Sets Excluded__c = true, Exclusion_Reason__c = reason. Writes change event.

verification_framework_proposal.impact: Constrains the c-verification-card spec: remove inline edit behaviours from 'Verified rows editable' specification. Verified rows should show the corrected indicator but route edits through the workspace modal, not inline.
verification_framework_proposal.specific_change: Change 'Verified rows editable' to 'Verified rows display corrected values with override indicator; edits route through workspace modal'

BH-1159.impact: Reinforces the page layout design: Proposed layout = read-only source fields + Verify action (aligned). Verified layout should NOT expose inline edit via the card — edits go through record page or modal.
BH-1159.specific_change: No change needed — BH-1159's Record Type page layout approach is compatible with read-only card

BH-1249.impact: Verification mini-Flows become the primary write path the card dispatches to. Card → Flow → service → record + change event. Flow handles audit field capture (Verified_By__c, Verified_Date__c).
BH-1249.specific_change: No change needed — BH-1249's Screen Flow approach is the correct write path

BH-1010.impact: Evaluator permission model confirmed: evaluators see the card as purely informational. VR_Evaluator_Assessment_Status prevents assessment on non-Submitted AARs. No card-level enforcement needed.

BH-1246.impact: Evaluator interaction is with AAR_Evaluation__c, not the verification card. Card shows verification state as context for the evaluator's assessment — no overlap.

BH-987.impact: VR_Attestation_Required fires on the standard write path. Card never bypasses it because card never writes.

BH-1126.impact: Field history tracking captures all changes made through the standard write paths. The card's read-only nature means every field-history entry corresponds to a deliberate edit — no noise from inline card saves.

decision_required: PM/architect to confirm: (1) c-verification-card is read-display + action-dispatch only, (2) all data edits route through workspace modal or record page, (3) verification actions dispatch to VerificationReconciliationService or BH-1249 Flows. If confirmed, update the Verification Framework proposal to remove 'Verified rows editable' from the c-verification-card spec.
